codes.definition: A numeric display whose source does not explicitly identify the counter role.
include_when: A number is visible and the source role label is absent or ambiguous.
exclude_when: The source explicitly labels the number as sold, orders, reviews, or another typed role.
positive_examples: A marketplace card shows 1.2k with no role label.
evidence_required: Adjacent source label and surface context

codes.definition: A public counter explicitly labelled by its source as sold.
include_when: The retained source label explicitly identifies the counter as sold.
exclude_when: Sold meaning is inferred from position, icon, endpoint name, or a bare number.
positive_examples: The card text explicitly states 500 sold.
counter_examples: A bare 500 appears beside a product.

codes.definition: The displayed price role is retained independently from temporal status.
include_when: Evidence distinguishes current, regular, from, promotional, discount, or unknown display roles.
exclude_when: Only acquisition method or observation time is available.
positive_examples: A current display price and regular strike-through price retain separate roles.
counter_examples: An API field is assumed current merely because it came from an API.
evidence_required: Source price label or layout evidence

codes.definition: Current advertised, historical observed, and unknown temporal states remain separate from price role.
include_when: Source temporal evidence supports current, historical, or explicitly unresolved status.
exclude_when: Temporal status is inferred solely from API, DOM, cache, archive, or other acquisition method.
positive_examples: An active official price page observed now, absent contrary history, supports current advertised at observed_at.
counter_examples: A cached response is labelled historical without source temporal evidence.

codes.definition: Product identity match does not establish selected-variant equivalence.
include_when: Product or item identity matches but variant attributes are absent, incomplete, or conflicting.
exclude_when: The same selected variant is supported by attributable variant identifiers and attributes.
positive_examples: Two records share a product ID but expose no matching size or color selection.
counter_examples: Product ID, variant ID, size, and color all match.
evidence_required: Variant identity evidence or explicit absence

codes.definition: Position is contextual display order and not demand, popularity, or national rank.
include_when: An item position is observed without an explicit source sort/ranking contract.
exclude_when: A source contract explicitly defines the retained ordering semantics and scope.
positive_examples: Item 1 on a generic marketplace result page is retained as display position 1.
counter_examples: A documented scoped ranking explicitly labels its metric and period.

codes.definition: A blocked environment does not disprove a technique when the same technique succeeds in a separately approved environment.
include_when: The technique is held constant and reviewed evidence shows an approved alternative environment succeeds.
exclude_when: The technique changed, the alternative environment was not approved, or no success evidence exists.
positive_examples: Rendered cards fail in cloud but the same rendered-card technique succeeds on approved Thailand Edge.

codes.definition: HTTP completed but the retained surface contained no stable usable business evidence.
include_when: Only an application shell or bootstrap UI is present after a bounded public attempt.
exclude_when: Stable attributable product or intended-scope evidence is retained.
positive_examples: The response contains only a static app mount and no product identity.
counter_examples: Rendered cards contain stable product identity and price.

codes.definition: A challenge or traffic-verification control stopped a bounded public attempt.
include_when: The visible or response evidence explicitly indicates traffic verification or challenge.
exclude_when: The page is merely empty, a normal application shell, or a technical transport failure.
positive_examples: A challenge page requests traffic verification and execution stops.
counter_examples: A normal SPA shell loads without a challenge marker.

codes.definition: Canonical detail URLs are discovered through official sitemap evidence and parsed at their detail surface.
include_when: Sitemap evidence yields canonical detail URLs and detail pages own attributable fields.
exclude_when: Only sitemap URLs exist without usable canonical detail evidence.
positive_examples: Official sitemap product URLs resolve to attributable product detail records.
counter_examples: A sitemap lists category pages only.

codes.definition: Public application-bundle clues support discovery only until semantics are independently validated.
include_when: Public bundles expose route, operation, or catalog-frontier clues with provenance.
exclude_when: Names or endpoints are treated as validated product data without response evidence.
positive_examples: A public bundle identifies a candidate discovery operation retained as a clue.
counter_examples: An endpoint name alone is asserted to own Product and Price.
